item.title: Real-world study of Oregon's nonmedical psilocybin program shows promise
item.description: Oregon was the first state to establish a legalized and regulated psilocybin industry. Since then, thousands have tried magic mushrooms. Here is the first data from the state's real life experiment.
item.content:encoded: Oregon was the first state to establish a legalized and regulated psilocybin industry. Since then, thousands have tried magic mushrooms. Here is the first data from the state's real life experiment.

item.title: Greetings from Trouville-sur-Mer, a beach town little changed since Monet painted it
item.description: The Normandy beach town of Trouville-sur-Mer is a two-hour train ride from Paris, but feels a world away, with English Channel breezes and the sound of seagulls screeching through the cobbled streets.

item.title: U.S. delays 50% tariff on Canadian imports. And, takeaways from Florida's primaries
item.description: President Trump has announced that the U.S. is delaying a 50% tariff on Canadian imports after reaching a deal. And, how progressive Democrats fared in Florida's primary elections yesterday.

item.title: How India's blocking of a film exposing real-life police abuses backfired
item.description: When Indian authorities scrubbed the biopic of activist Jaswant Singh Khalra, local villagers and activists turned its censorship into a grassroots movement.

item.title: Striking hospital employees sound alarm over workplace violence
item.description: In addition to pay, striking hospital workers say patient violence is an issue. Hospital workers are seven times more likely to be injured at work due to violent acts than the general working population.

item.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak reaches 5,000 cases as it outpaces response efforts
item.description: Government data showed the outbreak had so far recorded 5,021 cases, including 2,378 deaths. The outbreak has infected and killed more people at a greater speed than any other outbreak in history.

item.title: 15 states have laws that allow corporal punishment in schools. Here's where, and why
item.description: There is broad consensus among psychologists that corporal punishment can be harmful to children, but the U.S. has no federal laws banning it in public schools.

item.title: Elbridge who? How the name of a forgotten founder lives on in the word 'gerrymander'
item.description: Elbridge Gerry was an important early figure in the American Revolution, but his decision to approve a "gerrymandered" state legislative map inadvertently won him lasting infamy.
